subject.title: iOS app: node requests re-approval on every reconnect (token persistence bug)

question: Is the merged LAN QR bootstrap fix sufficient to close this issue, or should an iOS owner keep it open until current-main live reconnect proof separates token persistence from capability/permission reapproval drift?
rationale: The code and related PR prove one reported token-loss symptom is fixed, but the issue also reports manual setup and repeated node reapproval, which current source can still trigger through declaration changes without a live iPhone proof.

options.title: Keep Open For Live iOS Proof
options.body: Keep this issue open until a maintainer or iOS owner proves current-main reconnects do not create new pending node reapprovals after one approval.

options.title: Close As Covered By LAN Bootstrap Fix
options.body: Close only if maintainers accept https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98066 as covering the central user problem despite the missing manual-setup proof.

options.title: Split A Narrow Follow-Up
options.body: Close the bootstrap portion and open or link a narrower issue for iOS capability/permission reapproval drift if live proof shows that is the remaining root cause.

recommendation.title: Keep Open For Live iOS Proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a maintainer or iOS owner proves current-main reconnects do not create new pending node reapprovals after one approval.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue is already assigned to steipete and he has adjacent mobile bootstrap/auth history on the affected Swift gateway path.
